text:
The three days of travel have the character of a suspended sentence. During them there is no outward event; yet, for the meaning of the trial, all has been done. The servants are there, and the wood, the knife, and the fire; the instruments of the act are named before the act itself is reached. Obedience and horror remain in the same action, and neither is allowed to prevail. Faith here has the form of an ordered relation rather than of a feeling.

Placed beside the earlier promise, the difference between promise and trial grows narrower. Genesis 22 recalls Isaac as the child of the covenant, the one through whom the nations are to be blessed; that promise is made the matter of the test. The scene turns upon one word, hineni, "here I am," spoken by Abraham three times: to God, to Isaac, and to the angel. Each utterance bears another meaning, and each is dearer than the last. Presence itself has become the language of loss.
